body:
`/app/authors/9999999` (any id that does not exist) does not render an error
page. It renders a normal, fully functional author page whose *name* is the
string "Page not found":

    < Show all Authors
    AUTHOR   Page not found
    [Upload books] [All|Unread|Read] [Newest v] [Select] [refresh]
                     "No books here."

So the eyebrow label still says AUTHOR, the failure message occupies the slot
where the author's name belongs, and the toolbar below offers Upload / filter /
sort / select / refresh actions against an entity that does not exist. The page
then contradicts itself: "Page not found" in the title, "No books here." in the
body — two different explanations of the same condition, neither of which says
the URL is wrong.

Measured on `main`, 1440px and 390px, dark theme, logged in as admin. It is
stable, not a flash: identical at 3s, 10s and 25s. The API calls all return 200
(`/api/v1/authors` succeeds), so this is a client-side lookup miss being fed
into the normal render path rather than an error path.

Adjacent, checked in the same pass and NOT defects — recorded so nobody
re-derives them:

- `/app/book/9999999` resolves to a clean "Book not found" with a "← Library"
  link. Correct, though `<main>` is empty for the first several seconds before
  it appears.
- `/app/shelf/1` correctly reports "You are not allowed to view this shelf" off
  a genuine 403 from `/api/v1/shelves/1`.
- `/app/search?query=<no matches>`, `/app/archived` and the 404 route all
  render sensible empty states.
- No horizontal overflow in any of these states at 390px or 1440px.

The author page is the only one of the seven that fails this way, which is why
it looks like a missing 404 branch in that route rather than a systemic gap.

Method + full inventory: `notes/UI-SWEEP-INVENTORY.md` (outer workspace).
title: A nonexistent entity renders its error as the entity's own name
